parties.name: Alliance
parties.offer: End the two-child limit on benefits.
parties.excerpt: A wealth of evidence has demonstrated the link between the two-child limit in Universal Credit and higher poverty rates among larger families, with a harsh impact on children. Scrapping the policy would be one of the most efficient ways of reducing child poverty across the UK.
parties.scope: Selected two-child policy only. Resolution Foundation models Great Britain, not a full UK or party plan cost; Northern Ireland, the benefit cap and bedroom tax excluded.
parties.baseline: RF compares abolition with keeping the limit. Benefit take-up may differ in practice. Other benefit changes are excluded.
parties.year: RF estimate for 2024-25; cash, not a lifetime total. Research published before the election.
parties.status: 2024 election proposal; not current spending or a claim of policy now in force.
parties.costing: Independent estimate, not a party costing.
parties.assessment: one of the most efficient ways to drive down child poverty rates

costing.quote: Abolishing the two-child limit would cost the Government £2.5 billion in 2024-25

assessment.quote: one of the most efficient ways to drive down child poverty rates

parties.name: Traditional Unionist Voice
parties.offer: Raise employer National Insurance on foreign workers.
parties.excerpt: The National Insurance rate will be raised to 20% for foreign workers. This would incentivise businesses to employ British citizens whose National Insurance rate would stay at 13.8%. Essential foreign health and care workers would be exempt from the tax, as would businesses who employ 5 staff members and under.
parties.scope: Reform UK proposal quoted in TUV's manifesto; not a Northern Ireland-only revenue total. Health and care staff and small firms are exempt.
parties.baseline: Extra employer tax compared with the manifesto's standard-rate policy; no take-up or hiring-response model is supplied.
parties.year: Five-year projected revenue; no fiscal start year or price basis is stated.
parties.status: 2024 election proposal; not current spending or a claim of policy now in force.
parties.assessment: Unavailable here: No matched allowed-body assessment of this employer tax's design and exemptions was obtained. A review of Reform's full tax cuts is not that assessment.
